prompt:
Create a contemporary, polished desktop homepage UI mockup for FoodBridge at 1536×1024, edge-to-edge real website screenshot with crisp legible interface text, no device or browser frame. FoodBridge coordinates food sharing and separate waste collection in Sri Lanka. Preserve its name. All five roles must be equally discoverable: Donor, Recipient, Recycler, Volunteer, Admin. Recipients and recyclers can register for review; browsing and claims are not available yet. Admins sign in, never publicly register. Never invent metrics, live activity, endorsements, testimonials, maps, certifications, or deployed capabilities.

Visual direction: contemporary digital product with a photographic editorial sensibility. Bright white space, near-black evergreen typography, fresh pale green support and a controlled vivid lime accent. Precise modern sans-serif typography with a confident display scale and quieter regular-weight body copy. Generous margins, refined alignment, subtle borders, compact controls, and softly rounded photographic crops. Avoid the dated institutional look: NO road signs, numbered destinations, giant pictograms, thick green stripes, directory tables, glossy gradients, ornamental blobs, drop-shadow stacks, or repetitive role cards.
Composition A is photography-led, immediate and human. A quiet white masthead carries the FoodBridge wordmark, "How it works", "Community impact", and a compact "Sign in" control. The dominant element is one generously inset panoramic documentary-style photograph of adults in a contemporary Sri Lankan community kitchen preparing a crate of surplus vegetables. Natural light, authentic details, no visible branded uniforms, dignity rather than charity-advertising poses. Inside the photograph, readable white headline text says "Good food deserves another chance." with the short explanation "Food sharing and waste collection in Sri Lanka." The picture is a clearly illustrative scene, not an asserted real delivery.

A compact white role-selection panel overlaps the photograph's bottom edge. Label it "Find your place in FoodBridge"; give all five role choices equal visibility and a clear "Choose your role" next action. State "Admin access requires sign-in." Below, small readable text discloses "Recipient and recycler browsing and claims are not available yet." The viewport's lower region starts the distinct next section "One community. Different ways to help." with two short prose columns explaining food sharing and separate waste collection. Keep this recognisably a refined working website, not a campaign poster.
